summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=explore) with draft/explore-harness-tcp.go: an exploration of the last recorded unknown on the term-context line, namely whether the substitute stream layer was what let the heartbeat callback run concurrently with the main goroutine or whether the production transport behaves the same. The harness repeats the first check's interleaving verbatim — arm a StableStore wrapper, send a heartbeat-shaped AppendEntries so the real NetworkTransport classifies it and invokes the registered callback on its connection goroutine, hold that callback's CurrentTerm write, send a higher-term AppendEntries through the main loop on a second connection, then release the held write and read the term context and the store's write sequence — with the single change that both endpoints are NewTCPTransport instances bound to 127.0.0.1 and no substitute fabric exists; it skips cleanly when the TCP transport cannot bind. I ran it locally and it skipped, which is exactly why I submitted it as an exploration rather than a check: the local construction environment cannot bind loopback, so the output retained from the clean copy will show either the same regression over the production transport or that the transport was unavailable there, and either outcome records which of the two premises remains open instead of assuming one. Choosing explore also keeps the record clean: an exploration creates no Evidence and does not touch the unit the first check already completed, so a skipped run cannot disturb that confirmation — the cosmetic risk I weighed and avoided. The rationale states the question, the exact interleaving, the reason the substitute layer might matter, and that the exploration exists to distinguish the two premises. Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true. The run's standing is seven confirmed in-scope findings — the term regression through the transport callback, the two-leader overlap of one term, the acknowledged write the only replica does not hold, the client-future non-completion with two scenarios, the configuration index discrepancy, and the lease ending a leadership that a reachable quorum could still contact — plus one reviewed bounded negative about the overlap's persistence, one earlier retained exploration of the lease relation, and this exploration of the production transport, with the frontier otherwise limited to boundary and repair questions and the deferred surfaces about the snapshot commit context, the monotonic log store interplay, third-party heartbeat handlers and the nested modules.
